name: Reading Move and Combo Notation
summary: Read the shorthand used by guides, Trials, and combo lists.
description: Read the shorthand used by guides, Trials, and combo lists.

pages.title: Directions Before Buttons
pages.text: A direction is written before its button: {input:5A} is neutral A and {input:2B} is down B. {input:c.5B} means close standing B; {input:f.5B} means far standing B. {input:j.B} is airborne B, and {input:dj.B} is B after a double jump.

pages.title: Markers
pages.text: A ~ before a move marks an intentional delay. * means any listed button version, xN means a move must hit that many times, ? marks an optional step, and [SETUP] means the previous combo ended before the next part begins. (whiff) means the move should miss. IC (Instant Charge - a cancel you'll learn later in this tutorial) is written at the point where it is used.

tasks.prompt: What does ~ before a move mean?

feedback.delay: Right - a ~ tells you to pause a beat before that move.
feedback.repeat: Not quite - repeats are written xN. The ~ means delay.
feedback.optional: Optional steps get a ?. The ~ means delay.

tasks.prompt: What does x2 after a move mean?

options.label: The move must hit two times

feedback.hits: Right - the move has to actually connect that many times.
feedback.twice: Careful - xN counts HITS from one use of the move, not how many times you do it.
feedback.both: Nope - buttons are never written with xN. It counts hits.

tasks.prompt: What does [SETUP] between two parts mean?

options.label: The previous combo ended before the next part
Cancel into the next move faster

feedback.ended: Right - those are two separate combos glued together by a setup.
feedback.charge: Nope - EFZ notation never uses [SETUP] for charging.
feedback.cancel: Not this one - cancels are just written as the moves themselves.

tasks.label: Follow the shown sequence: {input:5A}, wait a moment, {input:5A}
tasks.prompt: Tap A, hold that pause on purpose, then tap A again - that little gap is the ~.
